coverage: ByteByteGo (Alex Xu) hosts four book-based courses: System Design Interview vols 1+2 (31 chapters), Object-Oriented Design Interview (14), GenAI System Design Interview (11) and Coding Interview Patterns (19 chapters, ~100 problems). Every SD chapter follows the same 4-step frame (scope, high-level design, deep dive, wrap-up) with dense block and sequence diagrams. Some chapters render in full for logged-out visitors. Others return only a title shell, so they are likely gated (marked paid). Chapters we didn't open are also marked paid, and their summaries say access wasn't checked.

refs.title: System Design Interview (vol 1 + 2) course
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: Public table of contents for the 31-chapter course: foundations (scaling, estimation, framework) and then about 25 case studies. Some chapters are readable without login; others look gated.

refs.title: A Framework For System Design Interviews
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: Time-boxed 4-step method (scope, high-level design plus buy-in, deep dive, wrap-up) with a do/don't list. It stresses writing assumptions down, sanity-checking with estimates and naming bottlenecks at the end.

refs.title: Scale From Zero To Millions Of Users
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: Grows one server step by step: split tiers, add a load balancer, DB replicas, cache, CDN, stateless web tier, multiple data centers, queues, metrics and sharding. The clearest model of incremental design evolution.

refs.title: Back-of-the-envelope Estimation
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: Powers-of-two and latency reference tables, a table of availability nines, and a worked QPS and storage estimate for a Twitter-like service, with tips on rounding and labelling units.

refs.title: Design A Rate Limiter
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: Compares five throttling algorithms (token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window, sliding log, sliding counter). Then moves from one middleware with a shared counter store to a distributed setup with race and sync fixes.

refs.title: Design Consistent Hashing
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: Explains why modulo hashing breaks when servers change, then covers the hash ring, virtual nodes for balance, and which keys move when nodes are added or removed. Diagram-heavy.

refs.title: Design A Key-value Store
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: A Dynamo-style walkthrough: CAP trade-offs, partitioning on a ring, replication, quorum tuning, vector clocks, failure detection and repair, and the read and write paths.

refs.title: Design A Unique ID Generator In Distributed Systems
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: Chapter on distributed ID generation (listed in the TOC). Logged out, the page returned no body, so it's probably gated. Content not sampled.

refs.title: Design A URL Shortener
refs.subject: system-design
refs.summary: Textbook 4-step case: traffic and storage estimates, two REST endpoints, a single-table data model, a hash-plus-collision vs base-62 trade-off table, and redirect caching.

refs.summary: Compares polling, long polling and WebSocket. Moves from one server to stateless and stateful services, chooses a KV store for history, refines message IDs and presence via heartbeats, and covers small-group fan-out.
